This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act', for short) has been filed by the Insurance Company being aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 18.09.2021 NC:
2025:KHC-K:6599-DB HC-KAR passed by the III Additional District and Sessions Judge and Member, MACT-IV, Vijayapura in MVC No.182/2017.

2. Facts giving rise to the filing of the appeal briefly stated are that on 20.03.2016 at about 4.30 The Branch Manager vs Sharada And Ors on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79047643/
2 p.m., when the deceased Ashok along with Basagond Jyothikhan and his son age of four years were proceeding on motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-28/B-3343 from Kotyal Dashyal road, near the land of Malleshi Sank, Badakalsab Takkod, at that time, the driver of the Tractor bearing registration No.KA-49/T-7605 came from side of land with high speed, which was being driven in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against the deceased.

sentences.text: As a result of the aforesaid accident, the deceased sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries.
3. The claimants filed a petition under Section 166 of the Act seeking compensation for the death of the deceased along with interest.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6599-DB HC-KAR 4.

On service of summons, the respondent Nos.1 and 2 appeared through counsel and respondent No.2 filed written statement denying the averments made in the claim petition and respondent No.1 fails to file the written statement.
5. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Claims Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter recorded the evidence.
The claimants, in order to prove the case, examined claimant No.1 herself as PW-1 and another two witnesses were examined as PWs-2 and 3 and got exhibited documents namely Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.16.
On behalf of respondents, one witness was examined as RW-1 and another witness was examined as RW-2 and got exhibited documents namely Ex.R1 to Ex.R.3.

The Claims Tribunal, by the impugned judgment, inter alia, held that the accident took place on account of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver, as a result of which, the deceased sustained injuries and succumbed to the injuries.

The Tribunal further held that the claimants NC:
2025:KHC-K:6599-DB HC-KAR are entitled to a compensation of Rs.15,73,802/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. and directed the Insurance Company to deposit the compensation amount along with interest.
Being aggrieved by the same, this appeal has been filed.
6. The learned counsel for the Insurance Company has raised the following contentions:
(a) Firstly, he contended that the accident occurred on 20.03.2016 and the complaint was lodged on 21.03.2016.

There is a delay of one day in lodging the complaint and he further contented that as per Ex.P.5- inquest panchanama, it was reported that the deceased while proceeding on two-wheeler was hit by unknown four- wheeler vehicle.
Therefore, he has contented that to make a false claim, they have implicated the said vehicle.
(b) Secondly, he has contented that considering the age and avocation of the deceased, overall compensation NC: 2025:KHC-K:6599-DB HC-KAR awarded by the Tribunal is on higher side.
Hence, he sought for allowing the appeal.
7. Per contra, learned counsel appearing for the claimants has contended that the accident occurred on 20.03.2016 at about 04.30 p.m.

Immediately thereafter, the injured was rushed to the hospital The Branch Manager vs Sharada And Ors on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79047643/
3 and the deceased was under treatment.

sentences.text:
Therefore, the complaint could not lodged on the same day,
but on the next day the complaint has been lodged i.e., on 21.03.2016, clearly mentioning the offending vehicle and its registration number.
The deceased was died on 25.03.2016 while undergoing treatment.
At the time of postmortem, the person who has given information did not mention the vehicle number that cannot be fatal to the claim made in Ex.P.5-inquest panchanam.

8. Heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties and perused the judgment and award of the Tribunal.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6599-DB HC-KAR 9.
It is not in dispute that the deceased Ashok was traveling in motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-28/B- 3343 as a pillion rider.
It is also not in dispute that he met with an accident on 20.03.2016 while under treatment he died on 25.03.2016 due to the accident and injuries.

10. Even though the accident has occurred on 20.03.2016 at about 04.30 p.m. as per the evidence of the parties and medical records, it is very clear that immediately he has been rushed to the hospital and he was under treatment till 25.03.2016 and he died on 25.03.2016.
Therefore, the family members who are taking care of the deceased were not in a position to lodge the complaint on the same day.
The complaint has been lodged on 21.03.2016 as per Ex.P.2 pursuant to that the police have registered an FIR as per Ex.P.1.
The complaint, which is lodged on 21.03.2016 there is specifically mentioned the offending tractor bearing registration No.KA-49/T-7605.

In the inquest panchanama, based on the opinion of the concerned NC: 2025:KHC-K:6599-DB HC-KAR panchas,
the vehicle number has not mentioned but the complaint which is lodged immediately after the accident, they have mentioned the vehicle number and FIR is also registered.
11. Considering these documents, the Tribunal has rightly held that driver of the tractor is negligent in causing the accident.
In respect of quantum is concerned, considering the age and avocation of the deceased and overall compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable.

Accordingly,
we proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
(i) The Miscellaneous First Appeal is hereby dismissed confirming the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6599-DB HC-KAR (ii) The amount in deposit is transmitted to the Tribunal forthwith.

Sd/-
(H.T.NARENDRA PRASAD) JUDGE Sd/-
